PUB-001.rationale: Appendectomy is not in the 48-month PED list or the first-year named-disease list, so it is a straightforward covered inpatient hospitalization. But room expense of INR 30,000 over 96h (4 days) implies ~INR 7,500/day, above the 1.0% of Basic Sum Insured (=INR 5,000/day) normal-room sub-limit, so a room-rent deduction applies. Ambulance charge of INR 1,200 exceeds the lesser-of-1%-SI-or-Rs.1000 ambulance cap, so a small further deduction applies.

policy_reference.clause: Room sub-limit: 1.0% of Basic Sum Insured/day
Ambulance charges capped at 1.0% of Basic Sum Insured or Rs.1000, whichever is less

PUB-002.rationale: Policy started 2026-01-01, claim date 2026-01-20 - only 19 days of coverage, inside the 30-day initial waiting period. continuous_coverage_months=0 and prior_insurer_continuous_years=0 mean neither of the two waiver conditions (prior continuous policy year with Us, or >=1 year continuous cover with another Indian insurer) is met. Viral fever is not an accident, so the waiting period is not otherwise bypassed.

policy_reference.clause: 30 days Waiting Period

PUB-003.rationale: treatment.pre_existing=true and continuous_coverage_months=27 is short of the 48-month pre-existing-disease waiting period. prior_insurer_continuous_years=0 means no portability credit reduces that 48-month clock, so the PED exclusion still applies in full.

policy_reference.clause: Pre-Existing Diseases definition (48 months)
PED not covered until 48 months of continuous coverage have elapsed

PUB-004.rationale: treatment.hospital_room_unavailable=true satisfies one of the two alternative Domiciliary Treatment conditions (non-availability of a hospital room), even though patient_cannot_be_moved=false. Domiciliary expenses (doctor_fees 25,000 + medicines/diagnostics 80,000 = 105,000) exceed the 20% of Basic Sum Insured aggregate sub-limit (=INR 100,000), so INR 5,000 is disallowed.

policy_reference.clause: Domiciliary Treatment definition
NB2: Domiciliary Hospitalization aggregate sub-limit of 20% of Basic Sum Insured

PUB-005.rationale: Cataract surgery is in the first-year excluded-disease list, but continuous_coverage_months=29 is well past the first policy year, so that exclusion no longer applies. Eye Surgery is explicitly named in NB4 as a procedure for which the 24-hour minimum stay is waived, so the 8-hour day-care admission still qualifies as covered hospitalization.

policy_reference.clause: NB4: 24-hour minimum stay waived for Eye Surgery and other named day-care procedures
First-year exclusion list includes Cataract, but only 'in the first year of operation'

PUB-006.rationale: documents omit itemized_bill (only claim_form + discharge_summary supplied), and evidence_context leaves hospital_registered and medical_necessity_confirmed as null/unresolved. The policy's Hospital definition and the expense sub-limits both require facts this case does not supply, so a safe decision cannot be made.

PUB-007.rationale: Cancer treatment is covered, but at sum_insured_inr=1,000,000: doctor_fees 300,000 exceeds the 25% cap (250,000); medicines/diagnostics/OT-category expenses of 500,000 exceed the 40% cap (400,000); room 80,000 over 96h (4 days, 20,000/day) exceeds the 1% cap (10,000/day). Multiple category-specific sub-limits apply simultaneously, each producing a deduction from the billed amount.

policy_reference.clause: Room sub-limit 1% of Sum Insured/day
Doctor/Surgeon fees capped at 25% of Sum Insured
Anesthesia/medicines/OT-category expenses capped at 40% of Sum Insured

PUB-008.rationale: Cosmetic surgery for a cosmetic condition falls squarely within the explicit exclusion for 'cosmetic or aesthetic treatment of any description' and 'plastic surgery except those relating to treatment of Injury or Disease' - the diagnosis and procedure text directly match the exclusion's own wording.

policy_reference.clause: Item 5: cosmetic or aesthetic treatment of any description excluded

PUB-009.rationale: expense_timing shows pre_hospitalization_days_before_admission=30 and post_hospitalization_days_after_discharge=60, exactly at (not exceeding) the policy's maximum windows, with same_condition_confirmed=true satisfying the 'same condition' requirement. All expense categories (room ~3,750/day, doctor_fees 50,000, medicines/diagnostics 100,000) are within their respective sub-limits, so no deduction applies.

policy_reference.clause: Pre-hospitalization up to 30 days, post-hospitalization up to 60 days
Pre-Hospitalization Medical Expenses must be for the same condition

PUB-010.rationale: continuous_coverage_months=8 is short of the current policy's own first year, but prior_insurer_continuous_years=1 with database_and_claim_history_received=true satisfies the waiver condition ('insured continuously... for at least 1 year under any other Indian insurer... We have received the database and claim history'), so the first-year Cataract exclusion is waived. Eye Surgery is separately covered under NB4 for day-care admissions under 24 hours.

policy_reference.clause: First-year exclusion waived with >=1 year continuous prior insurer coverage
Waiver conditional on Us receiving the database and claim history from the previous insurer
NB4: Eye Surgery day-care procedure

PUB-011.rationale: documents omit discharge_summary, and evidence_context explicitly leaves hospital_registered as null and hospital_minimum_criteria_documented as false, meaning the facility's compliance with the policy's Hospital definition (registration OR minimum bed count/staffing criteria) is neither confirmed nor disprovable from the supplied evidence alone as fully conclusive. The task itself frames this as an evidence-sufficiency question, so the safe action is to abstain rather than assume either outcome.

policy_reference.clause: Hospital definition: registration or minimum criteria

PUB-012.rationale: The policy DEFINES 'Unproven/Experimental Treatment' (Definitions, page 6) but the enumerated 'WHAT WE EXCLUDE' list (pages 8-10, items 1-21) contains no operative clause naming experimental or unproven treatment as excluded. A system that concludes NOT_ADMISSIBLE from the definition alone would be inferring an exclusion the policy text does not actually state - the safe action is to abstain pending underwriting/manual review of whether an unlisted exclusion applies.

policy_reference.clause: Unproven/Experimental Treatment definition - no matching operative exclusion found

CUST-001.rationale: prior_insurer_continuous_years=4 with database_and_claim_history_received=true reduces the 48-month PED wait to 0, but the reduction 'shall only apply to the extent of the Sum Insured under the previous health insurance Policy' (INR 100,000). Total claimed expenses (room 15,000 + doctor_fees 40,000 + medicines/diagnostics 90,000 + pre-hosp 5,000 + post-hosp 8,000 = 158,000) exceed that 100,000 ceiling, so the portion up to 100,000 is PED-wait-waived and admissible, while the remaining 58,000 is still subject to the full 48-month wait measured from this policy's own 6-month-old inception and is not admissible.

policy_reference.clause: PED waiting period reduced by continuous prior years of coverage
Reduction applies only up to the previous policy's Sum Insured

CUST-002.rationale: Standard covered appendectomy, well within all sub-limits (room ~4,000/day < 5,000 cap; doctor_fees 20,000 < 125,000; medicines/diagnostics 60,000 < 200,000). The patient's occupation and the hospital's parking availability have no corresponding policy clause and must not affect the decision.

policy_reference.clause: Room sub-limit 1% of Sum Insured/day (not breached)

CUST-003.rationale: The policy's 'Illness' definition requires 'a sickness or a disease or pathological condition leading to the impairment of normal physiological function.' An undiagnosed, cause-undetermined fatigue with only 'observation and monitoring' does not establish that this definitional condition is met, and no exclusion or coverage clause addresses undiagnosed/unconfirmed conditions directly - the system cannot confidently establish a policy-required condition from the evidence given.

policy_reference.clause: Illness definition requires impairment of normal physiological function

CUST-004.rationale: The facility is explicitly documented as having 6 in-patient beds in a town of population 400,000 (<1,000,000), below the policy's minimum of 10 in-patient beds required for such towns, and is not stated to be registered under the Clinical Establishments Act. Unlike a case with merely missing evidence, this evidence affirmatively shows the Hospital definition is not met, supporting a confident denial rather than abstention.

policy_reference.clause: Hospital minimum criteria: at least 10 in-patient beds in towns under 1,000,000 population

CUST-005.rationale: Both alternative Domiciliary Treatment conditions are explicitly false: hospital_room_unavailable=false and patient_cannot_be_moved=false. Neither of the two circumstances the definition requires is present, so the claim does not meet the Domiciliary Treatment definition and cannot be paid under that head.

policy_reference.clause: Domiciliary Treatment requires patient cannot be moved OR hospital room unavailable

CUST-006.rationale: ICU room expense of INR 100,000 over 4 ICU days = 25,000/day, which exceeds the 2% of Basic Sum Insured ICU sub-limit (=10,000/day) - a materially different, higher cap than the normal 1% room sub-limit. Doctor_fees (60,000 < 125,000) and medicines/diagnostics (150,000 < 200,000) are within their caps.

policy_reference.clause: ICU sub-limit: 2% of Basic Sum Insured per day
